chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who forgets and eats during the month of Ramadan, he said: He should complete his fast, for it is something which Allah fed him.
ai.seo_question: Does eating while forgetting invalidate the Ramadan fast?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'al-ghafilah' (forgetfulness) as a valid excuse for breaking the fast, distinguishing it from deliberate consumption. The Imam’s explanation that God 'fed' the person highlights the theological view that the act was divinely ordained rather than a personal failure, thereby preserving the integrity of the fast without requiring make-up or expiation. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for daily fasting practices and is often contrasted with the ruling for deliberate eaters.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Sirham, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who forgets, so he eats during the Month of Ramazan. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should complete his Fast. So, rather, it is something which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Fed it to him’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Dawud ibn Sarhan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who out of forgetfulness eats and drinks in the month of Ramadan, has said, ‘He completes his fast, it is only something Allah fed him.’”
